trust_decision.summary: When a messages object is compiled or merged, a language name must never resolve to an inherited property: the per-language target object is taken from the target only when it is an own property (Object.hasOwn) instead of `target[language] || {}`, which for language `__proto__` yields Object.prototype and for `constructor` yields the Object constructor, so every subsequent `target[language][code] = ...` writes onto that shared object.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading 'prototype pollution via a __proto__ language key in custom messages' goes to Messages.compile, the code that turns a `{ language: { code: message } }` object into Templates; the reported `.messages({['__proto__']: {...}})` example reaches exactly this line through Common.preferences (lib/common.js:183 -> lib/base.js:400).

fix_sites.entry_point: Joi.any().messages(obj) and .prefs({messages}) (lib/types/any.js:58 -> lib/base.js:400 -> lib/common.js:183); .validate(value, {messages}) / Joi.assert(value, schema, {messages}) (lib/index.js:224 -> lib/common.js:183); rule-level .message(obj) (lib/types/any.js:100-103)
Joi.extend({messages: {...}}) (lib/extend.js:22-23, merged over the base type's definition messages) and helpers.message(obj) in a custom validator (lib/validator.js:314 -> lib/base.js:849)
fix_sites.module_kind: message merge helper reached from the extension API and the validator helper API (lib/)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only dismissal available is for the merge() sink: a solver can argue Joi.extend({messages})/helpers.message(messages) are the caller's own configuration rather than attacker input, so 'custom messages' means the .messages()/prefs() compiler path and merge() can be left alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Per-language merging must accumulate: compile() is always called with the previously compiled messages object as its target (Common.preferences passes target.messages), so an already-own language object has to be extended in place. A fix that always allocates a fresh object, or that skips when the language already exists, silently drops earlier overrides for that language while the new pollution tests still pass.

O6_input_shapes: language name that resolves to an inherited object: `__proto__` (Object.prototype) and `constructor` (the Object constructor) - two different payload keys, only `__proto__` is named in the advisory summary
language value object whose keys are error codes mapped to plain strings, each wrapped in a Template
language value object containing 'root' or pre-built Template values, stored unchanged
flat (non-language) message maps, single strings and single Templates, which must keep compiling as before

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make decompile merge into an existing per-language object (`target[language] = target[language] || {}`) so a described manifest can be extended.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the exact mirror of compile()/merge() in the same file, and the describe path already rebuilds a messages map (lib/manifest.js:45-46); a maintainer adding overriding-decompile semantics would copy the same two lines and reopen the sink on the serialization side.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pre-create `messages[lang]` from the prefs language before rendering, e.g. `if (!messages[lang]) { messages[lang] = {}; }` on the read path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The read path already treats `messages[lang]` as possibly inherited and falls back to `messages[lang][code]` / `messages[lang]['*']`, so a maintainer 'normalizing' the language entry there would write onto Object.prototype for language `__proto__` in a handler the check never calls.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Build the alterations map from manifest keys with `alter[target] = adjuster` without an own-property/reserved-key guard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same 'user-controlled key into a fresh object' pattern as the message sink, inside the manifest rebuild path, and the repo already accepts this shape elsewhere.

O9_family: CWE-1321 prototype pollution through a user-controlled language key merged into a message map (object-integrity, library API)

O10_build.toolchain: npm; @hapi/lab 26 + @hapi/code test runner with a 100% coverage threshold (package.json:45); runtime deps are only @hapi/* packages
O10_build.project_tests: test/base.js:1988-2035 covers nested/flat language message overrides and invalid message values (the fix inserts its two new cases just before line 2030); test/extend.js:541-580 covers extension messages; test/validator.js:725 covers helpers.message with a string only, the object/language form is untested

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the reproduced path: in Messages.compile (lib/messages.js:53) skip or string-compare the language name (e.g. `if (language === '__proto__') continue;`) and verify with Joi.any().messages({['__proto__']: ...}), leaving Messages.merge (lib/messages.js:159, reached by Joi.extend and helpers.message) and the `constructor` language key untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Neighbouring, separately published prototype-key protections exist and were not pursued: object rename targets are rejected at lib/types/keys.js:986 (documented error object.rename.proto, API.md:4237-4239) and object values are cloned against a __proto__ key (test/types/object.js:108-127).
